observation.visible_scene: The excerpt contains two unrelated shots joined by a hard editing cut. The first shot (frames 1-4) shows a discarded, already-melted ice-cream bar lying on coarse grey asphalt: a pale wooden stick protrudes to the right, surrounded by cracked dark-chocolate shell fragments and smeared white/cream ice cream. The second shot (frames 5 onward) shows a pile of small golden breadstick-like snacks scattered on the same asphalt, with a white car bumper at the left and a black rubber tire at the right.
visible_changes: Frames 1-4 are essentially static; the only change is a dark out-of-focus shape at the top-left corner that is present in frames 1-2 and absent by frame 3.
A hard cut occurs between frame 4 and frame 5, replacing the ice-cream scene with the breadstick scene; there is no continuous transition between them.
From frame 5, the tire (marked 'ZERO' on the sidewall) translates leftward across the frame while its silver rim spokes rotate, indicating the wheel is rolling over the ground.

As the wheel rolls left, the breadsticks beneath the contact patch are progressively flattened and broken; crumbled, crushed pieces accumulate on the right side of the wheel (visible from ~frame 36 to 41).
The white bumper on the left moves out of view as the wheel/camera framing shifts, and the camera closes in so that the silver wheel rim and the tyre tread dominate the upper portion of later frames.
The un-crushed portion of the breadstick pile on the left stays roughly in place on the ground while the wheel advances over it.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the ice-cream bar's current melted state and the dark object at the top-left of frames 1-2 are not shown.
How the vehicle began moving, and what happens to the snacks after the wheel passes, lie outside the excerpt.
The relationship (if any) between the two shots is not established by the clip.
uncertain_details: The exact identity of the snacks (breadsticks vs. crackers) and of the ice-cream product is inferred from appearance only.
Whether the apparent tightening of the wheel in frame is due to camera movement or purely to the wheel's position is not fully separable from the background evidence.
The dark blurry shape in frames 1-2 is too out-of-focus to identify confidently.
